newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Alusuisse-Lonza has no plans to divest business.
newsitem.headline: Alusuisse-Lonza has no plans to divest business.

text.p: A senior executive with Swiss-based chemical firm Lonza SpA said on Tuesday its parent company, Alusuisse Lonza, had no plans to divest any part of its core business.

"Not that I know of," Andreas De Virgiliis, Lonza SpA's chief executive officer said when asked to comment on market talk that Alusuisse Lonza would spin off its aluminium business when its new chief executive officer Sergio Marchionne, who took office in April, announces his new business strategy next month.

"As usually happens in MNCs (multi national companies), the new CEO will review the current situation and deliver a strategy. But there is no substance (to rumours) of divestiture or things like that," he told reporters.
Alusuisse Lonza has three core businesses -- chemicals, Alusuisse Aluminium Products and Lawson Mardon Packaging.

De Virgiliis, who is also chairman of Lonza Singapore Pte Ltd, said the chemical arm was projecting total sales worldwide of Singapore $1.8-$1.9 billion (US$1.26-US$1.33 billion) in 1997, while total sales for the Alusuisse-Lonza group were about S$10 billion.
He was talking to reporters after the ground breaking ceremony of a US$125-million purified isophthalic acid (PIA) plant on Pulau Sakra, off southwest Singapore.

He said that when the Singapore plant starts after 1998, Asia's contribution to the chemical company's sales was targeted to grow to 30 percent from the current 10 percent, over the next three to four years.
PIA is a chemical intermediate used in the manufacture of unsaturated polyster resins and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) for use in plastic bottles and cans.
The plant, which is due for completion by end 1998, will produce 70,000 tonnes of PIA a year, De Virgiliis said.

"This investment demonstrates our enthusiasm to penetrate the fast growing Asia Pacific market, and to contribute to the growth of the PIA market which is expected to be an annual rate of seven percent until the year 2000," he said.
The Singapore plant is intended to provide for the majority of demand in Asia outside Japan, he said.
Lonza Singapore's general manager Giancarlo Angaroni said based on a market survey in 1994, Asian demand for PIA is 28,000 tonnes a year.
He also said global demand for PET was growing at 18 percent a year while Asian demand growth is more than 20 percent.
The plant under construction only occupies only 25 percent of its 10 hectare site and there are plans to expand it into areas such as research and biotechnology.
